elements.title: Social Emotional Development
elements.description: Social emotional development is the core of early care and education because it sets a firm foundation on which all other learning will take place.
elements.source_text: SOCIAL EMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

elements.title: Self-Awareness and Emotional Skills
elements.source_text: STRAND 1: SELF-AWARENESS AND EMOTIONAL SKILLS

elements.title: Relationships and Social Skills
elements.source_text: Strand 2: Relationships and Social Skills

elements.title: Self-Awareness
elements.description: The child demonstrates an awareness of self. Children develop a sense of personal identity as they begin to recognize the characteristics that make them unique as individuals and to build self-esteem.
elements.source_text:
Concept 1: Self-Awareness
The child demonstrates an awareness of self.
Children develop a sense of personal identity as they begin to recognize the characteristics that make them unique as individuals and to build self-esteem.

elements.title: Demonstrates self-confidence
elements.description: Acknowledges her own accomplishments and says, "I can hit the ball." Explains, "I'm learning how to take care of myself and my friends." Signs, "I can do it myself."
elements.source_text:
a.
Demonstrates self-confidence.
Acknowledges her own accomplishments and says, "I can hit the ball."
Explains, "I'm learning how to take care of myself and my friends."
Signs, "I can do it myself."

elements.title: Makes personal preferences known to others
elements.description: Chooses carrots over celery during mealtime. Tells friends, "I don't like that."
elements.source_text:
b. Makes personal preferences known to others.
Chooses carrots over celery during mealtime.
Tells friends, "I don't like that."

elements.title: Demonstrates knowledge of self-identity/autonomy
elements.description: Declares, "I'm the big brother," while looking at a family picture. Tells the teacher, "I'm at school while mommy is at work." Holds up three fingers and says, "I am this many."
elements.source_text:
C.
Demonstrates knowledge of self-identity/autonomy.
Declares, "I'm the big brother," while looking at a family picture.
Tells the teacher, "I'm at school while mommy is at work."
Holds up three fingers and says, "I am this many."

elements.title: Displays an awareness of similarities and differences between self and others
elements.description: Says, "My hair is curly and yours is straight." Points to shirt and then to friend's shirt, indicating that they are wearing the same color of shirt.
elements.source_text:
d. Displays an awareness of similarities and differences between self and others.
Says, "My hair is curly and yours is straight."
Points to shirt and then to friend's shirt, indicating that they are wearing the same color of shirt.

elements.title: Demonstrates developmentally appropriate cultural curiosity and responsiveness
elements.description: Wonders about a friend's seaweed snack and asks for a taste. The group widens the story time circle to make room for the child and their wheelchair. A guest speaker (parent) shares a storybook and song in their home language to the class.
elements.source_text:
e. Demonstrates developmentally appropriate cultural curiosity and responsiveness.
Wonders about a friend's seaweed snack and asks for a taste.
The group widens the story time circle to make room for the child and their wheelchair.
A guest speaker (parent) shares a storybook and song in their home language to the class.

elements.source_text: APPROACHES TO LEARNING STANDARD

elements.title: Language and Literacy
elements.description: Environments rich with print, language, storytelling, books, digital tools, and writing materials allow children to experience the joy and power associated with reading and writing, while mastering basic concepts of print.
elements.source_text: LANGUAGE AND LITERACY STANDARD

elements.title: Receptive Language Understanding
elements.description: The child demonstrates understanding of directions, stories, conversations, and nonverbal cues. Receptive language is the ability to understand or comprehend language that is heard or read.
elements.source_text:
Concept 1: Receptive Language Understanding
The child demonstrates understanding of directions, stories, conversations, and nonverbal cues.

elements.title: Expressive Language and Communication Skills
elements.source_text: Concept 2: Expressive Language and Communication Skills

elements.title: Vocabulary
elements.source_text: Concept 3: Vocabulary

elements.title: Demonstrates understanding of a variety of finger-plays, rhymes, chants and songs, poems, conversations, and stories
elements.description: Follows gestures and actions. Teacher asks, "Where would you like to play? It's time to work." Child points to blocks or answers, "Blocks." Teacher extends the interaction and builds on child's response by saying, "Oh, you want to play in the block area."
elements.source_text:
a. Demonstrates understanding of a variety of finger-plays, rhymes, chants and songs, poems, conversations,
andstories.
Follows gestures and actions.
Teacher asks, "Where would you like to play? It's time to work." Child points to blocks or answers, "Blocks."

elements.title: Engages actively in finger-plays, rhymes, chants and songs, poems, conversations, and stories
elements.description: Claps when prompted with, "If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands." Participates in story, Going on a Bear Hunt.
elements.source_text:
b. Engages actively in finger-plays, rhymes, chants and songs, poems, conversations, and stories.
Claps when prompted with, "If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands."
Participates in story, Going on a Bear Hunt.

elements.title: Demonstrates understanding and follows directions that involve one step, two steps, or multiple steps
elements.description: Places toy truck on shelf when adult says, "Please put the truck on the shelf." Responds to the directions, "Put the block on the table, put your paper in the cubby, and line up to go outside."
elements.source_text: C. Demonstrates understanding and follows directions that involve one step, two steps, or multiple steps.

elements.title: Expressive Language and Communication Skills
elements.description: The child uses verbal and nonverbal communication for a variety of purposes; to share observations, experiences, problem-solve, reason, predict, seek new information, and make connections.
elements.source_text:
Concept 2: Expressive Language and Communication Skills
The child uses verbal and nonverbal communication for a variety of purposes; to share observations,
experiences, problem-solve, reason, predict, seek new information, and make connections.

elements.title: Communicates needs, wants, ideas, and feelings through three to five-word sentences
elements.description: Engages intentionally in simple or multi-turn conversations with peers and adults at snack time. Talks with a peer about a trip to a park, another child utilizes sign language which includes social rules; pragmatics; age appropriate tone, and volume.
elements.source_text: a. Communicates needs, wants, ideas, and feelings through three to five-word sentences.

elements.title: Speaks clearly and understandably to express ideas, feelings, and needs
elements.description: Combines words into simple sentences - "Is it time to go home?" Or "More milk please." Says, "I want to go play at the water table."
elements.source_text: b. Speaks clearly and understandably to express ideas, feelings, and needs.

elements.title: Makes culturally relevant responses (both verbal and nonverbal) to questions and comments from others
elements.description: Exclaims, "I did it!" after teacher asks, "Did you get your jacket on?" Says, "I have a cat, too," after teacher shows a picture of a cat. Responds, "¡SÍ, mamá! I have my peanut butter sandwich," during drop off, after a parent asks, ¡Adiós! ¿ Tienes tu sándwich?
elements.source_text: C. Makes culturally relevant responses (both verbal and nonverbal) to questions and comments from others.

elements.title: Initiates, sustains, and expands conversations with peers and adults using open-ended responses
elements.description: Approaches peers and asks, "What are you making?" Says, "I went to the zoo." Teacher expands by asking, "What was your favorite animal?" Child replies, "The lion."
elements.source_text: d. Initiates, sustains, and expands conversations with peers and adults using open-ended responses.

elements.title: With modeling and support, child uses language that includes social rules; e.g., pragmatics, appropriate tone, volume, and inflection to express ideas, feelings, and needs
elements.description: Responds excitedly, "That's my favorite!" when an adult begins to read a book. Tells a classmate emphatically, "Stop, I don't like that!" or whispers in a classmate's ear during circle time.
elements.source_text:
e. With modeling and support, child uses language that includes social rules; e.g., pragmatics,
appropriatetone, volume, and inflection to express ideas, feelings, and needs.

elements.title: Uses culturally relevant responses such as eye contact, turn taking, and intonation while having conversations with adults and peers
elements.description: Uses turn-taking during conversations with peers and adults. Looks towards her friend, while speaking.
elements.source_text:
f. Uses culturally relevant responses such as eye contact, turn taking, and intonation while having conversations
withadults and peers.

elements.title: Recognizes when the listener does not understand and varies the amount of information to clarify the message
elements.description: Uses a different word to clarify the intended message when child realizes he has been misunderstood. Points to a picture to clarify his intent.
elements.source_text: g. Recognizes when the listener does not understand and varies the amount of information¹² to clarify the message.

elements.title: With modeling and support, uses increasingly complex phrases and sentences
elements.description: Says, "Let's put the cars up higher on the ramp so they will go really fast." Says, "I want to go home because my grandma is there."
elements.source_text: h. With modeling and support, uses increasingly complex phrases and sentences.

elements.title: Vocabulary
elements.description: The child understands and uses increasingly complex vocabulary.
elements.source_text:
Concept 3: Vocabulary
The child understands and uses increasingly complex vocabulary.

elements.title: Uses rich vocabulary across many topic areas
elements.description: Says, "Let me listen to your heart with a stethoscope" while in dramatic play. Reads The Very Hungry Caterpillar and exclaims, "I see a cocoon." The child uses new words or signs during play and other activities.
elements.source_text: a. Uses rich vocabulary across many topic areas.

elements.title: Figures out the meanings of unfamiliar words and concepts using the context of conversations, pictures that accompany text, or concrete objects
elements.description: Explains, "I am making skyscraper," while playing with the wooden blocks. Says, "I will get the colander to rinse the grapes" while playing in the dramatic play area.
elements.source_text:
b. Figures out the meanings of unfamiliar words and concepts using the context of conversations, pictures
that accompany text, or concrete objects.

elements.title: Uses category labels and names objects within a category; e.g., fruit, vegetable, animal, transportation
elements.description: Replies, "I want a carrot," when asked, "Which vegetable do you want?" Gathers a variety of animals and says, "I found a dog, two pigs, and a duck."
elements.source_text: C. Uses category labels and names objects within a category; e.g., fruit, vegetable, animal, transportation.

elements.title: Language
elements.source_text: STRAND 1: LANGUAGE

elements.title: Demonstrates understanding of and uses words that indicate position and direction; e.g., in, on, out, under, over, off, besides, behind
elements.description: Responds to the teacher's requests to return his car to the shelf, put blocks in the container, or stand beside a peer. Says, "I am standing between Billy and Rita."
elements.source_text:
d. Demonstrates understanding of and uses words that indicate position and direction; e.g., in, on, out,
under, over, off, besides, behind.

elements.title: Emergent Literacy
elements.source_text: STRAND 2: EMERGENT LITERACY

elements.title: Concepts of Print
elements.description: The child knows that print carries messages.
elements.source_text:
Concept 1: Concepts of Print
The child knows that print carries messages.

elements.title: Identifies signs, symbols, and labels in a variety of environments (environmental print)
elements.description: Points to a stop sign and says, "That says stop." Sees recycling symbol and says, "This is the recycling bin."
elements.source_text: a. Identifies signs, symbols, and labels in a variety of environments (environmental print).

elements.title: Demonstrates and understands that print conveys meaning and that each spoken word can be written and read
elements.description: Finds name on her placemat at lunch. Pretends to read a letter while playing Post Office.
elements.source_text: b. Demonstrates and understands that print conveys meaning and that each spoken word can be written and read.

elements.title: Recognizes that letters are grouped to form words
elements.description: Asks teacher to write name on paper. Groups letters together and asks, "What does this say?"
elements.source_text: C. Recognizes that letters are grouped to form words.

elements.title: Recognizes own written name and the written names of friends and family
elements.description: Reads job chart naming classmates. Picks up a name card and says, "This says Jose."
elements.source_text: d. Recognizes own written name and the written names of friends and family.

elements.title: Seeks information in printed materials
elements.description: Says, "We caught a cricket in our bug jar. Let's find a book about crickets." Looks at grocery advertisements while creating a shopping list.
elements.source_text: e. Seeks information in printed materials.

elements.title: Book Handling Skills
elements.description: The child demonstrates how to handle books appropriately and with care.
elements.source_text:
Concept 2: Book Handling Skills
The child demonstrates how to handle books appropriately and with care.

elements.title: Holds a book right side up with the front cover facing the reader and understands left to right and top to bottom directionality
elements.description: Turns the pages one page at a time to continue reading. Turns the book right side up before beginning to look at it, when handed a book upside down.
elements.source_text:
a. Holds a book right side up with the front cover facing the reader and understands left to right and top to
bottom directionality.

elements.title: Identifies where in the book to begin reading
elements.description: Finds the front of the book, the first page of the text, and the first word on the page. Points to the first page and says, "Start here."
elements.source_text: b. Identifies where in the book to begin reading.

elements.title: Understands a book has a title, author, and/or illustrator
elements.description: Makes a book and says, "My book is called My Mom, and I'm the author." Identifies that the illustrator draws the pictures in a book.
elements.source_text: C. Understands a book has a title, author, and/or illustrator.

elements.title: Phonological Awareness
elements.description: The child develops awareness that language can be broken in words, syllables, and smaller units of sounds (phonemes).
elements.source_text:
Concept 3: Phonological Awareness
The child develops awareness that language can be broken in words, syllables, and smaller units of sounds
(phonemes).

elements.title: Differentiates between sounds that are the same and different (e.g., environmental sounds, animal sounds, phonemes)
elements.description: Plays the game, Sound Bingo, and can differentiate between sounds - "That's a telephone." "That's a dog barking." Says, "Hey, the beginning of my name sounds like that /t/."
elements.source_text:
a. Differentiates between sounds that are the same and different (e.g., environmental sounds, animal
sounds, phonemes).

elements.title: Identifies rhyming words
elements.description: Shows thumbs up when two words rhyme in a poem, cat/hat. Points to pictures of words that rhyme.
elements.source_text: b. Identifies rhyming words.

elements.title: Produces rhyming words
elements.description: Sings, "Joy, noy, boy, loy, toy," while playing. Finishes the rhyme "The fat cat sat on the_."
elements.source_text: C. Produces rhyming words.

elements.title: Recognizes spoken words that begin with the same sound
elements.description: Exclaims Millie, "My name starts like Mel's name!" Selects man and mop as beginning with the same sound when presented with pictures of man, hat, and mop.
elements.source_text: d. Recognizes spoken words that begin with the same sound.

elements.title: Hears and shows awareness of separate words within spoken phrases or sentences
elements.description: Jumps when hearing a specified word in a story/poem. Claps each word spoken in a sentence "I like blocks."
elements.source_text: e. Hears and shows awareness of separate words within spoken phrases or sentences.

elements.title: Identifies and discriminates syllables in words
elements.description: Claps each syllable of a name during a name game or name song. (Ben-ja-min = clap, clap, clap) Takes a step for each syllable heard in a word. (hi-ber-na-tion = step, step, step, step)
elements.source_text: f. Identifies and discriminates syllables in words.

elements.title: Combines onset and rime to form a familiar one-syllable word with and without pictorial support
elements.description: Selects the correct picture of the cat when the adult says the name by segmenting it into its onset and rime components. (/c/ + /at/) Guesses, "Dog." when teacher says the onset and rime /d/+/og/.
elements.source_text: g. Combines onset and rime to form a familiar one-syllable word with and without pictorial support.

elements.title: Alphabet Knowledge
elements.description: The child demonstrates knowledge of the alphabet. Child identifies letters of the alphabet and produces correct sounds associated with several letters.
elements.source_text:
Concept 4: Alphabet Knowledge
The child demonstrates knowledge of the alphabet. Child identifies letters of the alphabet and produces
correctsounds associated with several letters.

elements.title: EMERGENT LITERACY
elements.source_text: STRAND 2: EMERGENT LITERACY

elements.title: Discriminates letters from other shapes and symbols
elements.description: Reads the book Chicka Chicka Boom Boom, and child points to the letter [a] and says, "That's the letter 'A' falling off coconut tree." Looks at an advertisement (environmental print) and the child points to the "W" for Walmart.
elements.source_text: a. Discriminates letters from other shapes and symbols.

elements.title: Matches and recognizes similarities and differences in letters, with modeling and support
elements.description: Traces the letter S and says, "The letter has curves." Says, "My name starts with a big A." The teacher says, "Let's make a letter A like the letter in your name." Then using playdough, the child and teacher create the letter A.
elements.source_text: b. Matches and recognizes similarities and differences in letters, with modeling and support.

elements.title: Recognizes an increasing number of letters, especially those in own name, familiar objects, family, and friends
elements.description: Names some letters while playing with alphabet stamps, magnets, cards, or puzzles. Says, "My name starts with an [l]." Paints the letter L like in her friend's name, while at the easel.
elements.source_text: C. Recognizes an increasing number of letters, especially those in own name, familiar objects, family, and friends.

elements.title: Demonstrates understanding of letters by producing letter forms using a variety of materials; e.g., playdough, blocks, marker, and paper
elements.description: Rolls out the first letter of their name, "K" in playdough. Writes letter "M" for "mom" on an envelope, while at the writing center.
elements.source_text:
d. Demonstrates understanding of letters by producing letter forms using a variety of materials; e.g.,
playdough, blocks, marker, and paper.

elements.title: Uses letter-sound knowledge, identifying the sounds of a few letters and producing the correct sounds for an increasing number of letters
elements.description: Writes name (Taylor) by making the "t" sound and then prints the letter. Says, "/S/, /s/, /s/, snake." when looking at a letter [S]. Replicates the letter sound when a teacher shows and says a letter.
elements.source_text:
e. Uses letter-sound knowledge, identifying the sounds of a few letters and producing the correct sounds for an
increasing number of letters.

elements.title: EMERGENT WRITING
elements.source_text: STRAND 3: EMERGENT WRITING

elements.title: Writing Processes and Writing Applications
elements.description: Children engage in a variety of writing activities and begin to convey meaning through their increasingly sophisticated marks. Children write to communicate ideas and to convey meaning. These skills include the understanding of print, the development of motor skills, and the generation of ideas.
elements.source_text:
Concept 1: Writing Processes and Writing Applications
Children engage in a variety of writing activities and begin to convey meaning through their increasingly
sophisticated marks. Children write to communicate ideas and to convey meaning. These skills include the
understanding of print, the development of motor skills, and the generation of ideas.

elements.title: In writing process, uses a variety of writing tools, materials, and surfaces to create drawings or symbols
elements.description: Draws random lines/scribbles on a page. Scribbles a note to mom, prior to leaving school. Draws to produce letter-like forms - creating a mock word - the child says, "This is 'Papa'." Listens to a book about where people live, and paints a picture of their home. Uses an interactive whiteboard to make an onscreen drawing of the snake from a story about snakes.
elements.source_text: a. In writing process, uses a variety of writing tools, materials, and surfaces to create drawings or symbols.

elements.title: Writes own name using letter-like forms or conventional print
elements.description: Writes own name on drawing. Writes own name from left to right on the sidewalk when playing with chalk on sidewalk.
elements.source_text: b. Writes own name using letter-like forms or conventional print.

elements.title: Intentionally uses scribbles/writing and inventive writing to convey meaning, ideas, or to tell a story; e.g., signing artwork, captioning, labeling, creating lists, making notes
elements.description: Asks, "What would you like to eat?" while playing restaurant and scribbles the order on a pad. Writes WLC M and says, "This says, 'Welcome'."
elements.source_text:
C. Intentionally uses scribbles/writing and inventive writing to convey meaning, ideas, or to tell a story;
e.g., signing artwork, captioning, labeling, creating lists, making notes.

elements.title: Forms letters starting with large motor (sky writing, paint brush and water, sidewalk chalk) progressing to fine motor (paper and writing utensil)
elements.description: Writes letters from name on the sidewalk with chalk. Writes letter-like forms on a page and says, "This is a note for my mommy."
elements.source_text:
d. Forms letters starting with large motor (sky writing, paint brush and water, sidewalk chalk) progressing to
finemotor (paper and writing utensil).

elements.title: Organizes writing from left to right, indicating a print awareness that letters cluster as words and words cluster into phrases or sentences by use of spacing or marks
elements.description: Plays at writing a message by placing spaces between the "words" on the page. Writes a series of letters and asks, "What word does this make?"
elements.source_text:
e. Organizes writing from left to right, indicating a print awareness that letters cluster as words and
wordscluster into phrases or sentences by use of spacing or marks.
